q: Which of the following statements regarding the Indian National Congress is correct?
options: The moderate and the extremist factions reunited at the Calcutta session of December 1906
explanation: The moderates and the extremists reunited at the Calcutta session of December 1906 and the same session saw the formation of the All India Muslim League.

q: The partition was:
options: annulled in 1911 and the Bengal was partitioned in 1912
explanation: The partition of Bengal was annulled at the Delhi Durbar of 1911 and the province was partitioned again in 1912 into the Bengal and the Assam and the Bihar and the Orissa.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Gandhi returned to India in January 1915 and the first Satyagraha?
options: The Gandhi returned to India in January 1915 and the first Satyagraha was the Ahmedabad in 1918
explanation: The Gandhi returned to India in January 1915 and the first of the three major satyagrahas of 1917-18 was the Ahmedabad mill strike, then the Champaran and then the Kheda.

q: In the context of the Indian Councils Act of 1919, which of the following is correct?
options: It provided for the provincial autonomy
It abolished the separate electorates and the direct elections
It provided for the franchise for the women
It provided for the separate electorates and the dyarchy
explanation: The Government of India Act of 1919 separated the central and the provincial subjects, introduced the dyarchy and separated the electorate for the first time.

q: The Hartal of 6 April 1919 was:
options: the first nationwide protest against the Rowlatt Act
explanation: The Hartal of 6 April 1919, the first all-India political protest, was called against the Rowlatt Act and the arrest of the Saifuddin Kitchlew and the Satyapal.

q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919 was:
options: ordered by the General Dyer in the Amritsar
explanation: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919 was ordered by the General Reginald Dyer who ordered his troops to fire on the peaceful crowd in the enclosed ground of the Amritsar.

q: The Khilafat agitation of 1919 was:
options: for the Sultan of Turkey and it coincided with the Non-Cooperation
explanation: The Khilafat agitation of 1919 demanded the restoration of the Sultan-Caliph of Turkey and it coincided with the Non-Cooperation Movement, and the two together gave the movement a broad mass base.

q: The movement included:
options: the boycott of the British goods, the surrender of the titles and the no-changers
explanation: The Non-Cooperation of 1920-22 combined the boycott of the foreign goods, the surrender of the titles and the honours, the refusal of the council elections, the leaving of the schools and the courts and the civil disobedience of the British.

q: The firing by the police at the Chauri Chaura of February 1922 led to:
options: the suspension of the Civil Disobedience
the start of the Quit India
the withdrawal of the Gandhi from the Congress
explanation: The firing by the police at the Chauri Chaura on 5 February 1922, in which 22 policemen were killed, led the Mahatma Gandhi to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement at the Bardoli meeting of the Congress in February 1922.

q: The Kakori train action of 1925 was:
options: the raid of the police station on the Upasana Express by the revolutionaries
the strike of the mill workers
explanation: The Kakori action of 9 August 1925, the raid on the police station on the Upasana Express near Lucknow, was the work of the revolutionaries like the Ram Prasad Bismil, the Ashfaqulla Khan and the Rajendra Lahiri.

q: The Simon Commission of 1928 had no Indian member and it was:
explanation: The Simon Commission, appointed in November 1927, had seven British members and no Indian and it was boycotted by all the political parties when it landed in Bombay.

q: The Lahore session of 1929 adopted:
options: the Purna Swaraj resolution and it was presided over by the Jawaharlal Nehru
presided over by the Motilal Nehru
explanation: The Lahore session of December 1929, presided over by the Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted the historic Purna Swaraj resolution and it authorised the non-violent struggle.

q: Civil Disobedience Movement began:
options: with the Dandi March on 12 March 1930 and it was the first mass movement against the British rule in India
explanation: The Civil Disobedience Movement began with the Dandi March of 12 March 1930 and it was the first all-India mass movement of the Indian nationalism.

q: The Pact of March 1931 provided:
options: for the suspension of the Civil Disobedience and the release of the prisoners in return for the Round Table Conference
explanation: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 5 March 1931 provided for the suspension of the Civil Disobedience and the release of the political prisoners, except those convicted of violence, in return for the Congress participation in the Round Table Conference.

q: The Poona Pact of September 1932 was:
options: between the Mahatma Gandhi and the B.R. Ambedkar
between the Gandhi and the Jinnah
between the Ambedkar and the Patel
between the Nehru and the Ambedkar
explanation: The Poona Pact of 24 September 1932 between the Mahatma Gandhi and the B.R. Ambedkar replaced the separate electorate for the Depressed Classes with the reserved seats within the general electorate.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the 1937 elections?
options: The Congress won an absolute majority in five of the nine provinces and the ministries were formed in seven
The Congress won all the nine
explanation: In the 1937 elections the Congress won an absolute majority in five provinces and the ministries were formed in seven and the League formed the government in Assam and Bengal.

q: Quit India Movement was:
options: launched on 8 August 1942 and it was the first movement in India with a mass participation
the first to use the non-violence
explanation: The Quit India Movement of 1942 was the first movement in India with the spontaneous mass participation and it saw the emergence of the Aruna Asaf Ali and the Jayaprakash Narayan as the leaders.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the INA?
options: The INA was founded in 1945 by the Nehru
The INA was a peasant force
The INA was revived by the Subhash Chandra Bose in 1943 with the Rash Behari Bose and the other leaders
explanation: The Indian National Army was revived by the Subhash Chandra Bose in 1943 in the Second World War with the Rash Behari Bose, the Prem Kumar Sahgal and the Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon and it had a woman, the Lakshmi Sahgal, in the Azad Hind cabinet.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the INA trials?
options: The INA trials at the Red Fort in 1945-46 provoked a nationwide agitation and the RIN mutiny
They were the trials of the British officers
explanation: The INA trials at the Red Fort, which began in November 1945, provoked a nationwide public agitation and the Royal Indian Navy mutiny of February 1946 and the British government withdrew the cases.

q: Cripps Mission proposed:
options: the dominion status and the constitution-making body after the war
explanation: The Cripps Mission of March 1942 proposed the dominion status after the war and the constitution-making body, and it failed over the Muslim League's insistence on the Pakistan.

q: Cabinet Mission proposed:
options: the three-tier federation and the grouping of the provinces and the Congress accepted it
explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 proposed the three-tier federation with the grouping of the provinces and the United Centre, and the Congress accepted it in July 1946 but the Muslim League rejected it.

q: Mountbatten Plan provided:
options: for the partition with the lapse of the paramountcy and the referendum clause for the princely states
explanation: The Mountbatten Plan of 3 June 1947 provided for the partition of India, the lapse of the paramountcy over the princely states and the referendum clause for their accession.

q: The Radcliffe Boundary Commission divided the Punjab and the Bengal and it published:
options: The Radcliffe Commission divided only the Bengal
explanation: The Radcliffe Boundary Commission, chaired by the Cyril Radcliffe, divided the Punjab and the Bengal and it published its award on 17 August 1947, five months after it was set up.

q: The Instrument of Accession was:
options: the act of the Indian Parliament
signed by the Indian states and the Sardar Patel and the V.P. Menon integrated them
explanation: The Instrument of Accession, a legal instrument of the accession of the princely states to India, was a joint work of the Sardar Patel and his secretary, V.P. Menon.

q: the Indian States is correct were:
options: There were 562 princely states and 9 provinces at the time of the independence
explanation: At the time of the independence there were 9 provinces and 562 princely states, and the process of the integration was completed with the accession of the last of them, the state of Hyderabad, in 1948.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The Hyderabad acceded to India is correct?
options: The Hyderabad acceded to India in 1948 after the Operation Polo
explanation: The Operation Polo of September 1948 secured the accession of the state of Hyderabad, the largest of the princely states by the area, and the Junagadh and the other states followed.

q: In the context of the Sikkim, which of the following is correct?
options: Sikkim became the 22nd state in 1975 after the referendum of 1973
explanation: The referendum of 1973 in Sikkim was against the monarchy and the state of Sikkim was formed in 1975 as the 22nd state of the Union.

q: The North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act of 1971 created the states of the North-East and the NEFA became:
explanation: The North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act of 1971 created the states of Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Nagaland and the NEFA became the Arunachal Pradesh.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Goa?
options: It was never a Portuguese territory
Goa was liberated on 18 December 1961 in the Operation Vijay
explanation: Goa, Daman and Diu were liberated from the Portuguese on 18 December 1961 in the Operation Vijay and the Goa Liberation Day is observed on 19 December.

q: In the context of the 23rd state, which of the following is correct?
options: the 23rd state in 1987 out of the Lushai Hills
explanation: The Mizoram became the 23rd state of the Union in 1987 out of the Lushai Hills of the former NEFA, following the Mizo Accord of 1986.

q: In the context of the Nagaland, which of the following is correct?
options: It was formed out of the NEFA
The Nagaland was the first state of the North-East to be formed on the tribal basis in 1963
explanation: The Nagaland, formed in 1963, was the first state of the North-East to be created on the tribal basis and it was the result of the Naga People's Convention of 1957.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the on the Fazz Ali is correct?
options: based on the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
based on the Fazz Ali Commission and it amended the First and the Fourth Schedules
explanation: The States Reorganisation Act of 1956, based on the Fazz Ali Commission's recommendations, amended the First and the Fourth Schedules to reorganise the states on the linguistic basis.

q: The Andhra State was:
options: created on 1 October 1953 and the Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956
explanation: The Telugu speaking Andhra State was created on 1 October 1953 and the present Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 by the addition of the Telugu districts of the Mysore state.

q: The Bombay state was:
options: divided into the Maharashtra and the Gujarat on 1 May 1960
explanation: The state of Bombay was divided into the Maharashtra and the Gujarat with effect from 1 May 1960 and the state of Punjab was divided into the Haryana, the Punjab and the Chandigarh.

q: Planning Commission was:
options: an extra-constitutional body set up in 1950 and it was chaired by the Prime Minister
explanation: The Planning Commission was set up in March 1950 by a resolution of the Cabinet and it was an extra-constitutional body chaired by the Prime Minister, and it was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.

q: Second Five Year Plan was:
options: the plan of the heavy industry and it was based on the Mahalanobis model
explanation: The Second Five Year Plan of 1956-61, based on the Mahalanobis model, had the emphasis on the development of the heavy industries and the rapid industrialisation.

q: New Industrial Policy announced:
options: Announced the delicensing, the foreign investment liberalisation and the reduction of the public sector
explanation: The New Industrial Policy Statement of 24 July 1991 announced the industrial delicensing, the liberalisation of the foreign investment, the reduction of the public sector and the phasing out of the MRTP.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the effort increase?
options: the effort to increase the milk
the effort to increase the fish
the effort to increase the exports
the effort to increase the foodgrain production with the high yielding varieties and the M.S. Swaminathan led it
explanation: The Green Revolution was the effort to increase the foodgrain production with the high yielding varieties of the wheat and the rice and it was led by the M.S. Swaminathan with the Norman Borlaug varieties.

q: led by the Verghese Kurien and it made:
options: led by the Verghese Kurien and it made India the largest milk producer
explanation: The White Revolution was led by the Verghese Kurien through the National Dairy Development Board and it made India the largest milk producer in the world.

q: The 1991 reforms and the creation of the SEBI and the disinvestment were:
options: under the P.V. Narasimha Rao and the Manmohan Singh
explanation: The 1991 reforms, the creation of the SEBI, the disinvestment and the reduction of the fiscal deficit were under the Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and the Finance Minister Manmohan Singh.

q: the NITI Aayog is correct was:
options: It was constituted in 2015 in place of the Planning Commission and it is a think tank without the plan funds
explanation: The NITI Aayog, constituted in January 2015 in place of the Planning Commission, is a collaborative think tank and it does not allocate the plan funds to the states.

q: The growth of the Indian economy in the 1990s and the 2000s was driven by:
options: the growth of the agriculture and the white revolution
the protection of the small scale industry and the import substitution
the decline of the foreign investment and the strict exchange controls
the growth of the IT and the services and the demographic dividend and the English language advantage
explanation: The Indian growth story of the 1990s and the 2000s rested on the 1991 liberalisation, the rapid growth of the IT and the service sector, the demographic dividend and the advantage of the English language.

q: the first of the independent India and the 2021 was:
options: the first of the independent India and the 2021 was the first after the 2011
explanation: The 1951 Census was the first census of the independent India and the 2021 Census was conducted after the postponement of the 2021 round because of the Covid pandemic.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Census?
options: The Himalayas and the Western Ghats
The Ganga and the Brahmaputra plains
The Deccan and the Chota Nagpur
The Cardamoms and the Coromandel and the Malabar and the Konkan
explanation: The Cardamoms, the Coromandel, the Malabar and the Konkan are the four divisions of the coastal region of the peninsular India.

q: In the context of the National Sample Survey, which of the following is correct?
options: The NSS conducted the surveys of the employment
The NSS is the statistical arm of the RBI
The NSS was the organisation that conducted the 2011 Census
explanation: The National Sample Survey Organisation, under the Ministry of Statistics, conducted the Periodic Labour Force Survey and it was the predecessor of the NSO that conducted the 2011 Census.

q: The Bhoodan movement of the Vinoba Bhave was:
options: the voluntary donation of the surplus land to the landless
the movement of the tenants against the landlords
explanation: The Bhoodan and the Gramdan movements of the Vinoba Bhave sought the voluntary and the maximum land reform with the landless as the recipients and it was the inspiration of the land reform legislation of the states.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The Ladakh is correct?
options: The Ladakh was a Union Territory in 2019 and it was part of the erstwhile Jammu and Kashmir
It is a part of the Himachal Pradesh
explanation: The Ladakh became a Union Territory in October 2019 along with the Jammu and Kashmir and it has a distinct culture and a sparse population.

q: Which of the following is correct in the case of the Article 370?
options: It gave the special status to the Jammu and Kashmir until it was abrogated in August 2019
It gave the special status to the Nagaland
explanation: The Article 370 gave the special status to the state of Jammu and Kashmir with the exception of the defence, the foreign affairs and the communications until it was abrogated in August 2019.

q: In the context of the Supreme Court directed, which of the following is correct?
options: It struck down the abrogation in 2019
It has not pronounced the judgment
It upheld the abrogation and the statehood was not restored
The Supreme Court directed the restoration of the statehood of the Jammu and Kashmir
explanation: In December 2023 the Supreme Court upheld the abrogation of the Article 370 and directed that the statehood of the Jammu and Kashmir should be restored with the assembly elections.

q: The committee that recommended the merger of the princely states with India was chaired by:
explanation: The Balbir Singh Seechewal headed the committee that examined the question of the merger of the princely states and he was a former Foreign Secretary of India.
